clue.text: Eccentric partisan

definitions.meaning: odd, departing from the normal pattern
a guerrilla fighter outside the regular army

explanation.definitionFit: An unconventional person is out of the ordinary, and a guerrilla soldier belongs to no regular army: both senses share the word.

clue.text: Correct yet again about the current recession

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning

indicators.note: a recession is a going back, so the word for the current is read backwards

parts.note: the tide is the current of the sea

explanation.surface: An economist revises a report on the latest recession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' turns TIDE into EDIT, which follows RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise a text a second time is to correct it once more.

clue.text: In time a little beast will make mistakes

indicators.note: the small animal sits inside the word for a period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a small animal

explanation.surface: Sooner or later a small creature will slip up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts RAT inside ERA, splitting it ER...A.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are the printing errors listed in a book, so mistakes is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Having to push maybe in the end

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the words before it could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone eventually forced to give a shove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' reworks TO PUSH. The definition is adverbial but the noun means the final result, what happens in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome or result of events is what comes about eventually.

clue.text: Mean to issue a statement before very long

parts.note: to aver is to declare or state firmly
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone intends to make an announcement before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb ('intend'), but it is the noun or adjective for a middle value; 'before' sets AVER ahead of AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics the mean is the arithmetical middle value of a set.

clue.text: Scoffed about the second being unduly complimented

indicators.note: the word for having eaten goes around the other piece

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed means fed
the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: Someone sneered at the runner-up while praising them far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' wants to mean mocked; here it means ate greedily, giving FED to wrap round LATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive praise is flattery, so someone praised too much has been buttered up.

clue.text: Made a live broadcast in years gone by

indicators.note: seed broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A programme went out live in the old days of television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like part of the TV picture but scatters MADE A LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediaeval describes the Middle Ages, a period long past, so it fits a phrase about bygone times.

clue.text: Watched outside event, as almost adult

indicators.note: the word for watched goes around the next word

parts.note: seen means watched or observed

explanation.surface: A teenager looked on from outside some occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts SEEN around EVENT: S + EVENT + EEN.
explanation.definitionFit: At seventeen a person is one year short of legal adulthood in Britain.

clue.text: Strip for run before church

parts.note: to flee is to run away
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A fugitive dashes off ahead of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' puts FLEE ahead of CE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to rob or swindle them of everything, as a sheep is shorn.

clue.text: Urge getting into the action when feeling low

indicators.note: the word for urge goes inside the word for an action

parts.note: a deed is an action
to press is to urge

explanation.surface: Pressure to act is getting someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' puts PRESS inside DEED: DE + PRESS + ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down in spirits is the same as being dejected or gloomy.

clue.text: Everybody out to make a hit

definitions.meaning: the call for all workers to walk off the job

explanation.definitionFit: A union calls a stoppage with 'everybody out', and the same word means to hit; both are senses of one word.

clue.text: It's just not true it can foil crooked characters

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A denial claims a story can outwit dishonest people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked characters' suggests villains, but 'crooked' rearranges the letters of IT CAN FOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A made-up story is invented, not factual.

clue.text: Abandon an unproductive piece of land

definitions.meaning: to leave someone or something behind

explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone in the lurch, and a barren sandy waste: two senses of one spelling.

clue.text: A dunderhead calling for the entree

parts.note: read as 'dunder head', the head or first letter of dunder
a mission is a calling or vocation

explanation.surface: An idiot with a vocation seeking access to a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' means a fool, but cryptically it is the head of 'dunder'. 'Entree' means entry here, not a main course.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is the right of access, the permission to enter somewhere.

clue.text: Contending with constituents is strange

indicators.note: the component letters of the following words are taken and rebuilt into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone argues that voters are behaving oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' suggests voters; here it means component parts, so the letters of IS STRANGE are reassembled.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend that something is so is to maintain or claim it.

clue.text: A flighty creature will supply all the runners with food

parts.note: the field is every competitor in a race
fare is food and drink

explanation.surface: A caterer feeds every horse in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: A FIELDFARE is a type of thrush; 'flighty' here means able to fly, not fickle.
explanation.definitionFit: This thrush is a bird, a creature of flight.

clue.text: Allow for rent

definitions.meaning: available to tenants, as a sign on a flat says

explanation.definitionFit: To permit, and to lease out property: two senses of one short word.

clue.text: Some cattle ambling about in a field

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A few cows wander around a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the join of 'cattLE Ambling'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a poetic word for a meadow or grassland.

clue.text: Add up for a child

definitions.meaning: to total figures, usually followed by up

explanation.definitionFit: To total a column of numbers, and a toddler: two senses of one word.

clue.text: Animosity can set the underworld boss corresponding

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld
like means similar or corresponding

explanation.surface: A gangland chief stirs hostility among those who resemble him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld boss' suggests a gangster, but it is Dis, ruler of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility toward someone is a feeling of aversion to them.

clue.text: Love to chatter about English work

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: the word for chatter goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: to prate is to chatter idly

explanation.surface: A lover gossips about some English task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside PRATE, giving PERATE after O.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or run, as a machine works.

clue.text: Fit for a little exercise

parts.note: PT is short for physical training

explanation.surface: Someone stays in shape with a short workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' says the exercise is shortened to its abbreviation PT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fitting or suitable is appropriate.

clue.text: Talk about the Spanish church dignitary

indicators.note: the word for talk goes around the Spanish article

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Gossip surrounds a high-ranking Spanish cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts EL inside PRATE, after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a bishop or other high-ranking cleric.

clue.text: One buys and sells most desirable models

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a trader deals in goods

explanation.surface: A dealer trades in the finest model cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' suggests toy cars or catwalks; here it means perfect examples to aim for.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards of perfection one aspires to.

clue.text: Hail to thee, — Spirit! Bird thou never wert." Shelley (To a Skylark)

definitions.text: Hail to thee, — Spirit! Bird thou never wert." Shelley (To a Skylark)

parts.words: Hail to thee, — Spirit! Bird thou never wert." Shelley (To a Skylark)
parts.note: the opening line of Shelley's poem with its adjective blanked out: fill in the missing word

explanation.definitionFit: The poem opens by greeting the skylark as a joyful, carefree spirit, the sense of the missing adjective.

clue.text: Look for the small change in a party

indicators.note: the coin goes inside the word for a group

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
p stands for penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: Someone eyes the coins carried by a political group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P inside SECT: S + P + ECT, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the appearance or look of something, as in a house with a southern aspect.

clue.text: A Kipling novel turned up festive occasion for the emperor

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: Kim is a novel by Rudyard Kipling
an ado is a fuss or to-do, a celebration with commotion

explanation.surface: A Kipling book appears at a party for the emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns KIM into MIK; ADO follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese emperor is titled the Mikado, as in Gilbert and Sullivan's opera.

clue.text: Sensible article is well put together

indicators.note: the letters are assembled anew into a well-built word

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is praised for being neatly constructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well put together' reads as praise but rearranges ARTICLE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical, level-headed view takes things as they are.

clue.text: Started as a bigwig in the Canterbury area

indicators.note: the toff is placed in the region, written after its abbreviation

parts.note: Canterbury is in Kent, in the south-east of England, SE
a toff is an upper-class swell

explanation.surface: A grandee began his journey in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Canterbury is a cathedral city in Kent, the south-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off is to begin a journey.

clue.text: An American stock holder

parts.note: reads as a US shareholder, but the stock is livestock on a ranch

explanation.definitionFit: A rancher in the US keeps cows, livestock rather than shares.

clue.text: They have to make news or bust!

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Journalists must get a scoop or go bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' reads as bankrupt but breaks up NEWS OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who possess things have them.

clue.text: Keeping note X turned it on

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: turned means the short word just after it is reversed

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to a message marked X and switches it on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses IT to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the act of holding on to something.
